title: applyJoinRules labels opt-out and deny-rule removals with skip reason untrusted-sender, which is untrue for an opt-out
evidence: Opt-out of event e2 with a trusted sender a@x.com: applyJoinRules(sel([item e1, item e2]), {version:1,ownDomains:[],rules:[]}, {state:{approvedSenders:[],approvedDomains:[],optedOutEventIds:["e2"]}}) -> skipped[0] = {reason:"untrusted-sender", detail:"join-rules veto: meeting-opt-out (rule opt-out:e2)"}. Consumers found by grep on 60b57d2: schedule-tick.ts:216 describeSkip prints [reason]+detail only; auto-record-policy.ts:300 projectWebinarSelection passes skipped through verbatim to CLI JSON; apps/api/src/routes/brain.ts:100 has its own operation-reason vocabulary that does NOT include untrusted-sender. Nothing branches on the reason today, so the mislabel is cosmetic now; it becomes a defect the moment the wiring unit persists skipped items or an operator UI maps untrusted-sender to an approve-this-sender action.
fix_direction: Wiring-unit precondition: add SkipReason values (e.g. rule-refused and meeting-opted-out) in webinar-types.ts before applyJoinRules is called from schedule-tick, and map opt-out -> meeting-opted-out, deny-rule -> rule-refused, invalid rule set -> rules-unevaluable; or the wiring unit must prove no consumer branches on untrusted-sender. Verify against the repro above.

title: Opt-out recorded under a calendar event id is missed when the same webinar is scheduled via a different source id (every-webinar dedup keeps only one id)
evidence: selectAutoRecordItems({everyWebinar:true, now:"2026-10-10T09:50:00Z", leadMinutes:15, calendarEvents:[{id:"calX",title:"Weekly sync",organizer:"o@x.com",meetingUrl:"https://zoom.us/j/123456789?pwd=a",startTime:"2026-10-10T10:00:00Z",endTime:"2026-10-10T11:00:00Z"}], candidates:[{id:"g1",title:"Webinar: Intro to X",senderEmail:"o@x.com",status:"approved",meetingUrl:"https://zoom.us/j/123456789?pwd=a",startTime:"2026-10-10T10:00:00Z",endTime:"2026-10-10T11:00:00Z"}], trustedSenders:{emails:[],domains:[]}, alreadyScheduled:[]}) -> toSchedule=[{sessionKey:"webinar-0db97b0c0169e74955cdd108", sourceId:"g1"}], calX skipped needs-review. applyJoinRules(thatResult, {version:1,ownDomains:[],rules:[]}, {state:{approvedSenders:[],approvedDomains:[],optedOutEventIds:["calX"]}}) -> toSchedule.length 1 (NOT removed). The person opted out of calX; the same meeting still gets an unattended join through the gmail candidate. The unit cannot know the two ids are one meeting.
fix_direction: Wiring-unit precondition: opt-outs must be resolved to the webinar identity (url+start) or all source ids aliased to the surviving item before/while applying the veto (e.g. pass every sourceId that collapsed into a webinar sessionKey as extra candidate ids), with a regression test using the repro above. Library change optional: accept an aliases map in the context.

title: Invalid rule set removes EVERY scheduled item of the tenant; policy needs an explicit Approver decision before wiring (record-every-webinar D-058 / ISS-376)
evidence: applyJoinRules(sel([item e1 a@x.com, item e2]), {version:2,ownDomains:[],rules:[]}) -> kept=0 removed=2 detail "join-rules veto: rules could not be evaluated (failing closed)"; same for null, {}, [], "str", and state null/{}. A valid EMPTY rule set and undefined rules keep everything (same reference).  The detail does not carry the validation error, so an operator cannot tell which rule is broken.
fix_direction: Wiring-unit precondition: Approver confirms fail-closed-for-whole-tenant (this unit ruled it acceptable for an unwired library because failing open would join meetings a corrupt deny list was meant to refuse) or fail-open-with-loud-alert; the wiring must log the JoinRuleSetValidationError message once per tick, and the behaviour must default off behind a flag that leaves today behaviour unchanged.
